heading: Appendix F — Running an Experimental Study: From Question to Credible Evidence

figures.alt: Three panels name and explain noncompliance, attrition, and spillovers or interference. Noncompliance separates treatment assigned from treatment received; attrition separates randomized participants from those whose outcomes are observed; spillovers connect one person's treatment to another person's outcome. A fourth panel defines intention-to-treat as comparison by original assignment and states that it does not itself resolve attrition or spillovers.
figures.caption: Figure F.3: Three distinct problems in a randomized evaluation: treatment receipt can differ from assignment, follow-up can leave outcomes missing, and treatment can affect other people. An intention-to-treat comparison retains the original assignment groups; missingness and spillovers require additional attention.
